sentences.text: Ptychodus was an extinct genus of shell-crushing lamniform sharks that lived during the Cretaceous period.
At least 16 species of Ptychodus are considered valid, ranging from about 2 meters in length for the smallest to 10 meters for the largest.
A Ptychodus jaw could contain up to 550 teeth, with 220 on the lower jaw and 260 on the upper jaw.
Ptychodus teeth were historically misidentified as the palates of porcupinefish for a long time.
The youngest known remains of Ptychodus date to around 75 million years ago.
The first Ptychodus teeth found in Kansas were reported by Leidy in 1868 near Fort Hays.
The first confirmed record of Ptychodus whipplei teeth from South America was reported in 2026 from the Itamaracá Formation in Brazil.
Analysis of vertebrae suggests Ptychodus species lived long lives, grew slowly, and produced large offspring in small litters.
Ptychodus is classified within the family Ptychodontidae.
Fossils of Ptychodus teeth are found in Late Cretaceous marine sediments worldwide.
Records suggest Ptychodus originated in the Western Interior Seaway before spreading across Cretaceous seas globally.
